answer: Minimum inter-arrival spacing admits each identity's actions only after randomized 20–45 second gaps, queueing bursts. An attacker may seed an orchard of clones, but every clone pays its own warm-up delay and must sustain compliant gaps. Traffic-shape checks at the forge flag bursty duplicates before routing. Steady nectar flows earn faster admission, so clones mimicking them still burn parallel slow channels.
